title: Adding events to courses
intro: Semester → Courses → Events. Research into how instructors create and edit scheduled events inside a course (simulation sessions, live classes, labs, exam slots): date and time, room and equipment, which scenarios run, which learner groups attend, facilitators, capacity and recurrence. The calendar overview and communicating dates to learners is sub-module 10; scenarios (05) and learner groups (04) are neighbouring concerns.

questions.title: Event creation surface: inline in course vs. global calendar with course tag
questions.answer: Two surfaces coexist, and the strongest evidence shows them side by side in one product. Kajabi schedules sessions inline under a coaching product (mobbin:1680974d, flow mobbin:c497ddd0) and, separately, runs a Marketing → Events calendar with no product link at all (mobbin:64f56885). Luma is the global-with-tag model: the create form starts with "Create under [calendar]", so the container is chosen at creation (refero:1843). Acuity splits the reusable class type from the act of offering an instance on a date (refero:9859). Calendly (refero:df769788) and TravelPerk (refero:5222) are global-only lists with one Create button. Circle is the cautionary case: it has course spaces, yet its create-event form sits under the global Events tab (mobbin:b360aa69), and its "scheduled" course space flow is lesson drip, not bookable sessions (mobbin:f92f2d5a). For an instructor building a course calendar the inline surface wins because the course is implied context; the global calendar should be a filtered view with the course as tag. No reference shows the reverse direction (a course page listing events created from a global calendar), which is exactly the seam module 10 has to close.

questions.title: Linking content and groups to the event (and whether that link is visible both ways)
questions.answer: Only Understory shows an explicit content → event step: "+ Event" opens "Select the experience", and the form is then pre-filled with capacity, location, resources, rooms and guides (refero:12719). Workable gets the same effect by opening the event from the record, so the title and context are pre-populated (mobbin:da2ca788). HubSpot is the one product that treats the group as an object: the event side panel has "Associated campaign" and "Lists" sections, though both are empty in the capture (mobbin:0135db7d). Luma (mobbin:787e8052) and Rise (mobbin:1caacacf) link the event to individual attendees, with statuses, not to a cohort. Nothing in the set shows the link from the other side (a scenario or group page listing its sessions), and nothing attaches a learner group as a unit. Preply is the counter-example: a one-to-one lesson with nothing to link (refero:9226). For Essentials the event form should start from the scenario, as Understory does, accept learner groups as objects, as HubSpot lists do, and both the scenario and the group should list their sessions, which has to be designed without a reference.

questions.title: Recurrence and series editing (this / following / all)
questions.answer: Recurrence at creation is table stakes: a repeat rule with frequency, weekdays and an end condition appears in Zoom (mobbin:b85c076b), Understory (refero:12705), Amie (mobbin:68dd9778) and Skiff, whose flow shows the customise modal and the instances rendered on the calendar (mobbin:d5d0e3c0). Edit scope is thinner than expected: Amie (mobbin:1c7e609d) and Motion (mobbin:1eb73c81) both ask "this event / all events", and no reference in this set offers the three-way "this and following". Luma is the only product that builds a series from an existing single event: "Create multi-session event" → add recurring sessions (cadence, number of weeks, weekday chips) or a manual session list → the event shows "+9 sessions" (refero:1848). Acuity is the counter-example: rescheduling one class instance shows a plain date/time panel with no scope question (refero:9872). Simulation sessions rarely repeat identically because groups rotate through scenarios, so Luma's explicit session list is a better fit than a bare repeat rule; the two-option scope dialog is still needed when a whole series moves.

questions.title: Resource conflicts (room, facilitator, equipment) surfaced at creation
questions.answer: Every conflict message found is a soft warning shown after the fact, never a block inside the creation form. Acuity reopens a class with a yellow banner naming the resource ("uses resource Room #5") and still saves (refero:9868). Fresha warns that the staff member is not working at that time with Apply still enabled (mobbin:ac5e971e). Clockwise says "I can schedule this meeting, but there is a conflict for Sam" (mobbin:671e0870). 7shifts batches the check at publish time, counting conflicts and offering "fix them for me" (mobbin:8796902e). Google Workspace has a room and equipment picker with capacity but no availability feedback (mobbin:0a1650e1); SavvyCal's "Ignore calendar conflicts" toggle implies detection exists elsewhere (mobbin:44fd56e6); Zoom only complains at join time (mobbin:2ef394f0). Understory models resources with quantities (refero:12709) yet its session modal shows no conflict feedback at all (refero:023aed7b), the counter-example. No product shows equipment-specific conflicts. For a simulation centre, rooms, manikins and facilitators are the scarce resources, so the pattern to adopt is warn-don't-block, but moved into the form as live per-resource availability, which no reference demonstrates.

questions.title: Capacity, sign-up and attendance model
questions.answer: Three sign-up models appear. Self sign-up: Aboard's single Attend toggle (mobbin:4fa0df58) and Partiful's RSVP with plus-one, where spots decrement per person, 20/20 to 18/20 (refero:10204). Approval-gated: Luma's guest list moves people from Pending approval to Going under a cap of 1,000 (mobbin:68dc9ea7). Host-added: SavvyCal lets the organiser invite a guest after scheduling (refero:3371). Capacity is a numeric field with a "no limit" option in Understory (refero:12706) and per ticket tier plus an event total in Eventbrite (mobbin:c0b0ead0). Attendance is always marked by the host: Posh toggles a guest to Checked in (mobbin:4022cce6); Lyssna offers Mark as completed / No-show and auto-completes after five days (mobbin:8a3407fe). No reference shows a waitlist or attendee self check-in. In Essentials attendance is mostly assigned through the learner group, so the useful borrowings are the capacity field with a no-limit option, Posh's check-in and Lyssna's automatic resolution of unmarked sessions.

questions.title: Time zone and duration handling
questions.answer: An explicit time-zone selector is the norm. Microsoft Teams leads the form with the zone, then start and end with a computed duration and an all-day toggle (refero:9746). Cal.com shows the zone on both the availability page and the booking page (mobbin:8a0d881c, refero:3492). Kajabi (mobbin:5de887fe), SavvyCal (mobbin:9a8fc4f4) and Clockwise (mobbin:1fe20459) pair the zone with duration presets and an availability grid. Zoom is the exception on duration, taking free hours and minutes (mobbin:f6032c78). Homerun uses start plus a duration dropdown and shows the zone only as a read-only label (refero:7186), the counter-example to the explicit selector. Upwork is the only product that previews the other party's local time ("2:16 PM GMT+8, 2h ahead") (mobbin:55d0a62f). Simulation sessions happen in a physical centre, so one institutional zone shown as a label is enough, and duration should default from the scenario's running time (module 05), which makes Homerun's start-plus-duration model the closest fit.

references.title: Defining an appointment type globally, then offering/scheduling it onto the calendar
references.question: Q1
references.take: Acuity separates defining the reusable class/appointment type (global catalog) from the act of scheduling an instance onto the calendar, a two-step global-catalog pattern.

references.title: Scheduled events dashboard listing all events with a global Create button
references.question: Q1
references.take: Calendly lists all scheduled events in one global dashboard with a single Create action, rather than event creation living inside a specific course/project context.

references.title: Create event form with date/time, repeats, and end date configuration
references.question: Q1
references.take: Circle's create-event form opens under the global Events tab, not inside a course space: date/time, repeat rule and end date, with no course field.

references.title: Creating a course space (scheduled) - 14-step flow with date selection and group assignment
references.question: Q1
references.take: Full scheduled course creation showing date/group selection within course setup; demonstrates inline event scheduling with group context.

references.title: Sessions tab with list of scheduled sessions and reschedule functionality
references.question: Q1
references.take: Sessions listed inline within course detail view, each with reschedule action; shows inline session management.

references.title: Create event form with title, when field, timezone, and repeat configuration
references.question: Q1
references.take: Event form with title, datetime, timezone, and recurrence interval selector; clean course event creation.

references.title: Scheduling a coaching session - 8-step flow with calendar and availability setup
references.question: Q1
references.take: Complete session scheduling flow from course coaching context with calendar, availability setup, and time slot selection.

references.title: Creating an event and picking/creating the owning calendar (course tag equivalent)
references.question: Q1
references.take: Luma requires choosing or creating a "calendar" (the container/tag) as part of event creation, showing a global-calendar-with-tag pattern rather than an inline-in-course surface.

references.title: My lessons view with Schedule lesson button and upcoming lessons list
references.question: Q1
references.take: Inline lesson scheduling within course/instructor context; Schedule lesson CTA creates events within course.

references.title: Creating a team event from a global Events area, then viewing its detail overview
references.question: Q1
references.take: TravelPerk events are created from a dedicated global Events area and then reviewed on a detail overview page, separate from any specific project/course context.

references.title: Event details with linked attendees, associated campaign, and lists sections
references.question: Q2
references.take: Event panel showing attendees, associated campaign link, and lists; demonstrates rich linked content around event.

references.title: Event invite stats showing attendee list with acceptance status and invitations
references.question: Q2
references.take: Invite stats panel showing all attendees with acceptance status; demonstrates two-way visibility of event-attendee relationship.

references.title: Rescheduling a lesson from the student's lesson list, tied to a specific lesson/tutor
references.question: Q2
references.take: One-to-one lesson reschedule (list → menu → new slot) with nothing to link: no content selection, no group.

references.title: Event details with participant list and bidirectional event-participant linkage visible
references.question: Q2
references.take: Event details panel with participant avatars and names; shows event-to-person links within event context.

references.title: Creating a calendar event by selecting an existing "Experience" and adding a resource
references.question: Q2
references.take: The event creation flow requires selecting an existing Experience (content) to link the event to before adding capacity and resources, showing an explicit content-to-event link step.

references.title: Interview event creation with linked candidate profile and role information
references.question: Q2
references.take: Event (interview) with linked candidate and role visible; shows bidirectional link (candidate has event, event has candidate).

references.title: Rescheduling one appointment instance from the weekly calendar (single-instance edit)
references.question: Q3
references.take: Rescheduling one class instance opens a plain date/time panel with no "this / all" question: single-instance editing only.

references.title: Repeat dialog with weekly frequency, specific days, and end date selection
references.question: Q3
references.take: Repeat modal allows frequency (every 2 weeks), day selection checkboxes, and end date picker with visual end-date display.

references.title: Update recurring event dialog with this event vs all events options
references.question: Q3
references.take: When editing recurring event, shows choice between 'This event' and 'All events' radio buttons to scope changes.

references.title: Converting a single event into a multi-session series and adjusting the cadence
references.question: Q3
references.take: Luma treats a multi-session event as a conversion step from a single event, with its own modal for adding sessions manually or configuring a recurring cadence.

references.title: Update recurring event modal with this event vs all events scope selector
references.question: Q3
references.take: Modal displays 'This event' and 'All events' options (radio buttons) when updating recurring series, allowing scope control.

references.title: Flow: Customizing a recurring event with edit scope and recurrence modification
references.question: Q3
references.take: Repeats toggle → frequency → "Customize recurring event" (every / on / ends) → instances rendered on the calendar; no edit-scope dialog appears in the captured frames.

references.title: Setting a custom recurrence rule and end date when adding a date/location to an experience
references.question: Q3
references.take: Custom recurrence is its own dialog with an explicit end-date picker, separate from the base date/location entry, letting the end condition be set independently of the start.

references.title: Recurring meeting settings with frequency dropdown, weekday selection, and end date options
references.question: Q3
references.take: Recurring meeting setup shows repeat frequency (Weekly), occurs on weekdays (Sun-Sat checkboxes), and end date with occurrence count option.

references.title: Scheduling warnings dialog showing shift conflicts and employee overboking alerts
references.question: Q4
references.take: Warning modal displays exception counts (6 Exceptions, 0 Conflicts, 1 Overtime warning, 0 Unassigned Shifts) before publishing schedule changes.

references.title: Opening an event and seeing a conflict warning that another event is blocking the same resource/time
references.question: Q4
references.take: The event detail panel shows an explicit conflict warning naming the blocked resource (a room) and time when opening a class that overlaps another booking, directly surfacing a resource conflict at the point of viewing/editing.

references.title: Scheduling conflict warning showing multiple conflicting time blocks and unavailability alerts
references.question: Q4
references.take: Calendar view displays conflict alerts ('I can schedule this meeting, but there is a conflict', 'Sam has conflicts that I can't fix') with visual indicators.

references.title: Team member availability conflict warning when scheduling service
references.question: Q4
references.take: Warning alert shows 'Alex Smith is not working between 7:00am and 7:45am' when staff member is unavailable during booking slot.

references.title: Add resource dialog in event creation showing room selector with labels and capacity info
references.question: Q4
references.take: Resource management dialog lists available rooms/equipment (Meeting room A, TV Screen, Video conferencing, Power outlets) with capacity details.

references.title: Availability override dialog showing conflict with attendee calendar constraints
references.question: Q4
references.take: Modal 'Override availability' displays attendee conflicts and allows forcing time despite availability constraints.

references.title: Setting up a resource type with follow-up duration and quantity for booking
references.question: Q4
references.take: Resources are modeled as their own type with a defined quantity, which is the mechanism by which the system could prevent double-booking, though no live conflict warning is shown at creation.

references.title: Centered modal for creating/editing an event/session with no resource-conflict field shown
references.question: Q4
references.take: Create/edit session modal has a "Resources: 1 rule" field but no availability or conflict feedback anywhere in the form.

references.title: Meeting conflict detection showing already scheduled meeting in same time slot
references.question: Q4
references.take: Dialog alerts 'You are already in another meeting' with option to start meeting anyway or handle conflict.

references.title: Confirming attendance for an event
references.question: Q5
references.take: Two-step flow: event details with attendance status and 'Attend' button, then confirmed attendance state with checkmark.

references.title: Event tickets with capacity limits and availability
references.question: Q5
references.take: Tickets tab shows capacity (0/25 general, 0/20 student), sold status, and option to edit capacity.

references.title: Event page with guest list and registration status
references.question: Q5
references.take: Shows guest list with capacity (cap 1000), pending/invited/attended status, and role-based permissions for attendance.

references.title: Marking session attendance as completed
references.question: Q5
references.take: Host workflow: sessions list with 'mark attendance' prompt, marking sessions complete/no-show, automatic 5-day auto-mark for absent sessions.

references.title: RSVPing to an event and adding a plus-one from the event details screen
references.question: Q5
references.take: Sign-up is modeled as an RSVP action with an explicit plus-one addition, showing attendance capacity being tracked per invitee rather than a generic ticket count.

references.title: Guest marked as checked in
references.question: Q5
references.take: Three-step guest flow: status change to 'Set Checked In', confirmation, and guestlist with checked-in badge.

references.title: Reviewing a scheduled event and inviting an additional guest
references.question: Q5
references.take: Attendees can be added to an already-scheduled event after the fact via an "Invite a guest" modal, showing sign-up/attendance as an ongoing editable list rather than fixed at creation.

references.title: Editing the capacity of a date/location block for an experience
references.question: Q5
references.take: Capacity is edited as its own discrete step directly on the date/location block, independent from other event fields.

references.title: Rescheduling a booking by picking a new date and time slot from availability
references.question: Q6
references.take: Time slots are generated from a week/day availability grid tied to the organizer's working hours, implying time zone conversion happens behind the slot grid rather than via a manual selector.

references.title: Availability scheduling with time zone and buffer settings
references.question: Q6
references.take: Availability page shows time zone (Asia/Jakarta), weekly hours (9:00-17:00), date overrides, and buffer settings.

references.title: Booking a meeting with time zone and duration options
references.question: Q6
references.take: Four-step booking flow: duration preset selection, date/time picker with time zone (Asia/Jakarta), confirmation, and success message.

references.title: Scheduling an interview: picking a template, date, start time, duration, and location
references.question: Q6
references.take: Start time plus a duration dropdown (60 min); the time zone is only a read-only label, not a selector.

references.title: Session scheduling with time zone and duration
references.question: Q6
references.take: Create session modal shows time zone picker (New York), duration indicator (30 minutes), calendar picker, and time slot selector.

references.title: Creating a community event from an empty events state through the full new-event form
references.question: Q6
references.take: The new-event form surfaces start date/time controls with default values pre-filled, reducing the time-entry burden inside a long creation flow.

references.title: Scheduling with duration presets and time zone
references.question: Q6
references.take: Availability form with time zone selector (US/Canada), duration options (30/15 min presets), and time grid display.

references.title: Scheduling a meeting across time zones
references.question: Q6
references.take: Chat flow: proposing meeting date/time picker with multiple time zone support (America/New_York), duration selection.

references.title: Schedule meeting with time zone, duration, and recurring options
references.question: Q6
references.take: Meeting form shows time zone selector (GMT-7:00 Pacific), duration with hour/minute inputs, and recurring meeting controls.
